grand_strategy.reading: Lebanon's grand strategy since Aoun's election (9 January 2025) and Salam's government (February 2025) is the strategy of a state trying to become the owner of its own war and peace. The aim is simple to state: one army, one decision on war, Israel out, money in. The means are borrowed: American brokerage, Saudi and Qatari money, European training, Egyptian ideas, a UN mandate that is ending. The 2026 war showed the gap between the declared monopoly and the actual one: Hezbollah fired on 2 March in spite of the cabinet's own ban, and the state paid in dead, displaced and territory. Beirut's answer is not to fight Hezbollah (the army will not, and the state would not survive it) but to move the country's major patrons into a sequence in which Israeli withdrawal, army deployment and donor money arrive together. That is why it signed a framework with a state it does not recognise and why it avoids the word normalisation. It is a strategy of patience and bargaining from weakness, and its test is the pilot zones: if Israel does not withdraw from a place the army has actually cleared, the Shia community will keep its arms for good and the state's whole case will fall. Syria and the Gulf matter because they take the land and sea borders and the money out of Iran's hands; Russia, China and Turkey are marginal. This card is dated 12 October 2026, before the next round of Israel-Lebanon military talks planned for 20-21 October and the EU's formal decision on the army mission.

stances.note: The state's posture toward its own armed actor. The cabinet decided on 5-7 August 2025 to put all arms under state control and on 2 March 2026 banned Hezbollah's military activity and ordered the army to stop launches; the army declared phase one south of the Litani complete on 8 January 2026. Aoun calls disarmament non-negotiable. Not 'adversary': the state does not seek Hezbollah's destruction, refuses to force disarmament (a Hezbollah MP warns of civil war), keeps Hezbollah and Amal ministers in cabinet, and says Hezbollah may join a national security strategy after an Israeli withdrawal. Competing interests and open friction, no will to destroy: rival. No source uses the word 'rival'; the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C). Trend cooling: the March 2026 ban and the framework signed over Hezbollah's rejection. Bond - kin: the same citizens and the same confessional system; Hezbollah is a Lebanese party in parliament.

stances.note: Adversary or rival? Rival. Israel occupies about 65 Lebanese towns and villages (an estimated 570-600 sq km) and has killed more than 4,300 people in Lebanon since 2 March 2026, and Beirut has no diplomatic relations and does not normalise. But the Lebanese state is not seeking Israel's destruction: it signed on 26 June 2026 a US-brokered framework whose first point affirms each side's right to exist and states an intent to end the state of war, it negotiates directly (ambassadors in Washington from 14 April, rounds in Rome in July and August, another in October), Aoun speaks of a security agreement that could lead to peace, and the state fights Hezbollah's war-making on paper. The mortal enemy in this triangle is Hezbollah, which the state grades separately. Trend stable: direct talks warm the process, the continuing strikes and the occupation cool it. Bond - grievance: occupation of 1978-2000, the 2024 and 2026 wars. Ceasefire of November 2024 preceded; the April 2026 truce and the framework followed.

Against that it treated the cabinet decision of Aug 2025 'as if it did not exist', walked out three times, threatens a 'Karbala-like' battle and demands the 2026 framework's 'downfall'. Why not rival: the cooperation is structural (the Shia share of the system, state cover, donor money) and no source has Hezbollah targeting state institutions; Lebanon's own card grades Hezbollah rival, an asymmetry that is deliberate. It becomes a rival if the army moves by force or Hezbollah leaves the cabinet. No source uses the label; our reading, confidence C. Bond - kin: the same citizens and the same confessional system.
